host: Apple M4 arm64, macOS 26.5 (25F71), 10 logical CPUs
interpretation: ObjectRecordSpace reserves exactly 16,777,216 × 32 B = 512 MiB virtually. Source has one such allocation; vmmap shows one contiguous 512 MiB MALLOC_LARGE range at both stages, split into a 128 MiB mapped subrange and a 384 MiB reserved subrange. The matching size and unique source allocation strongly associate this range with ObjectRecordSpace, although vmmap does not label the Rust owner.

The 128 MiB mapped subrange resident size grows 15.8 → 31.5 MiB (+15.7 MiB) from setup to after 300 runs. A separate 2,160 KiB MALLOC_LARGE allocation appears after work, of which 1,728 KiB is resident; together these explain the aggregate MALLOC_LARGE resident growth of +17.3 MiB.
MALLOC_SMALL residency grows another 18.2 MiB. These allocator-region totals locate where residency grows but do not separate live arrays, metadata, fragmentation, or unrelated allocations.
limits: This is an uninstrumented OS mapping snapshot, not the profile-memory structural census.
The work sample is after the 300th run and before TearDown; it is current RSS at a stopped process, not a sampled intra-run peak.
The custom materialized input and ps/vmmap metrics are not interchangeable with the stock-harness qualification RSS.
